claims.text: Properly manufactured CFRP load-bearing components will significantly reduce structural weight relative to conventional aerospace aluminum-alloy components.
CFRP components will maintain or exceed the overall mechanical performance of conventional aerospace aluminum alloys.
Commercially available carbon-fiber prepregs can be combined with a suitable polymer matrix for the proposed application.
Established composite layup and curing processes can be used to fabricate CFRP structural components.
The proposed performance comparison is applicable under variable temperatures, cyclic loading, and impact scenarios relevant to aerospace service.
Carbon-fiber alignment and distribution within the polymer matrix mediate stress transfer.
Appropriate carbon-fiber alignment and distribution enhance the mechanical integrity of CFRP.
Carbon fibers inherently possess high tensile strength and stiffness.
The polymer matrix has an energy-dissipative character.
The combination of strong, stiff carbon fibers and an energy-dissipative polymer matrix produces a higher strength-to-weight ratio than aluminum alloys.
The combination of carbon fibers and the polymer matrix provides improved fatigue resistance relative to aluminum alloys.
CFRP components will reduce weight by approximately 20–30% relative to conventional aerospace aluminum-alloy components.
CFRP components will match or surpass the tensile strength of conventional aerospace aluminum-alloy components.
CFRP components will match or surpass the fatigue life of conventional aerospace aluminum-alloy components.
CFRP components will match or surpass the impact resistance of conventional aerospace aluminum-alloy components.
Composite fatigue and impact behavior can be sensitive to manufacturing variations and long-term environmental exposure.
The proposed conclusions may not extend to applications with radically different environmental exposures or manufacturing constraints.
